_comment: EXP-28: the mix changes DURING a condition, at a constant arrival rate.
EXP-27 measures three mixes as three separate conditions, which answers
whether the partition PolyServe computes differs between them. It cannot
answer what the transition costs, because within a condition there is no
transition. This file replays a trace whose class column steps m1 -> m2 ->
m3 -> m1 in 2-minute segments while the arrival rate stays flat at 40 req/s,
so the only thing moving is the composition.
Why 2-minute segments: PolyServe recomputes its allocation every 10 s and
applies a change only after 2 consecutive rounds agree, so it reacts in
about 20 s. Reassignment itself is free but draining is not -- migration is
off in these runs, so a server that changes tier keeps serving its old
tier's in-flight requests, and an agent request runs for tens of seconds.
A 2-minute segment leaves PolyServe correct for most of the segment and
wrong across the boundary, which is the quantity being measured.
The rate is flat on purpose. The Azure-shaped version (rate and mix both
moving) is the 1-hour run; separating them first is what makes the 1-hour
